17-13-0303-C (1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans - Zoning Map Amendment - SUBSTITUTE
4456-4458 North Western Avenue, Chicago, Illinois

Proposed Zoning: B3-3 Community Shopping District
Lot Area: 5,356.80 square feet

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is seeking an elective Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment with
Administrative Adjustment relief, pursuant to Section 17-13-0303-D of the
Chicago Zoning Ordinance, in order to permit the construction and
occupancy of a new five-story eight-unit mixed-use building, with onsite
accessory parking for eight automobiles, at the subject property. The
programming for the proposed new development calls for the establishment
of a single commercial unit (1,093 square feet) on the ground floor —
fronting Westem Avenue and wrapping along the Sunnyside Avenue
corner, thereby activating both public ways. The 2™ through 5® Floors of
the proposed new building will feature a total of eight (8) dwelling units —
two units, stacked side by side, per floor. There will be interior parking for
a total of eight (8) automobiles and at least (8) eight bicycles situated within
the rear of the ground floor, with access directly off of the Public Alley. The
new proposed improvements will be masonry in construction, with the
building measuring 54 feet-10 inches in height.

(A) _ The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 16,057 square feet (Total) (3.0 FAR)
*1,093 square feet (Ground Floor Commercial)

*The Applicant is seeking an Administrative Adjustment to reduce the minimum
required ground-floor commercial floor area by approximately 19% - from 1,339
square feet to 1,093 square feet, pursuant to Sections 17-3-0305-A and 17-13-1003-X
of the Zoning Ordinance. Such reduction is necessary in order to allow for the provision
of highly demanded moderately-sized (i.e., “affordable”) commercial space with
maximum street exposure, which is intended to be occupied by a small local business
that will service the residents of the immediate area, as well as families that attend the
nearby schools and public park, while still too allowing for the provision of one-to-one
secured (garage/interior) vehicular parking for each of the new large format (family-
oriented) dwelling units, on this significantly substandard-depth site. Such modest
reduction will not have any adverse impact on the health, safety or welfare of the
general public and adjacent property owners. To the contrary, the commercial unit as
designed and proposed was widely supported by the community and residents in the
area, as a “benefit” to public safety and welfare, by activating the ground floor of this
vital corner property with a locally owned and operated business intended to directly
serve the immediate neighborhood.

(E)

The Project’s Density (Lot Area Per Dwelling Unit): 8 _ units (669.6 square
feet per dwelling unit)

The amount of off-street parking: *8 total automobile spaces; 8 bicycle spaces

*The Applicant is seeking an Administrative Adjustment to increase the Minimum
Automobile Parking Ratio for this Transit-Served Location (TSL), from four parking
spaces (50%) to eight parking spaces (100%), so that the residents of each of the
proposed three-bedroom “market-rate” dwelling units will have secured parking for
their own personal vehicle, pursuant to Sections 17-3-0308(4) and 17-13-1003-EE of
the Zoning Ordinance. Based on market demand and community feedback, the
proposed new large format (‘family-oriented’) units will be offered for-sale as
“condominiums.” The market data for this neighborhood clearly shows that all owner-
occupied units of this size/format are deeded at least one off-street parking space and
similar units without such accommodations are unviable.

Setbacks: a. Front Setback: 0 foot-4 inches
b. *Rear Setback: 24 feet-4 inches

*The Applicant is seeking an Administrative Adjustment to reduce the required rear
setback for residential use by not more than 50% - from 30 feet to 24 feet-4 inches,
pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-I of the Zoning Ordinance. The proposed 20% (5 feet-
8 inches) reduction of the required rear setback is necessary to overcome the
significantly substandard lot depth plaguing the subject site, which such menacing
topographic condition (hardship) prevents the Applicant from constructing a strictly
code-compliant multi-unit residential building that features functional and ‘standard’
sized floor plates. The Applicant designed the proposed new multi-family building with
considerable deference to the immediately adjacent improvements, and — too, drawing
inspiration from the character and functionality of the other buildings that comprise the
subject block, almost all of which such other buildings enjoying similar reduced rear
yard depths. *{The footprints of ALL - but one of the buildings that comprise the subject
block of Western Avenue - west side, occupy the entire depth of their respective site —
ie., ZERO rear setback.]

c, Side Setbacks:
North: 0 feet-1 3/16 inches
South: 0 feet-0 inches

Building Height: 54 feet-10 inches (underside of roof truss)

7

(F) Pedestrian Street Fagade — Transparency: 227 square feet (83% - Western Avenue)
*250 square feet (39% - Sunnyside Avenue)

The Applicant is seeking an Administrative Adjustment to the Pedestrian Street
Building Facade Standards — Transparency, to allow for a reduction in the minimum
amount of required transparent window area for the Sunnyside Avenue facing fagade
— from 380.4 square feet (60%) to 250.4 square feet (39%). [Section 17-3-0504-C;
Section 17-13-1003-Q] Just under half of the ground floor — at the rear, is occupied by
the attached garage (vehicular and bicycle parking for the residents of the new building),
which is a “non-commercial use.” As such, that same portion of the side elevation - on
Sunnyside Avenue, lacks large (floor-to-ceiling) transparent windows, so that all of the off-
street parking for the new development/building is not visible from the right-of-way of such
pedestrian street.
